key_insight: TokenLight encodes distinct lighting factors as compact attribute tokens, enabling precise, continuous, and independent control of multiple illumination properties in a single relighting model. This frames image relighting as conditional image generation conditioned on interpretable lighting tokens.
problem_solved: Existing relighting methods struggle to give users fine-grained, composable control over multiple illumination attributes (intensity, color, ambient, diffuse, 3D light position) simultaneously and continuously; TokenLight provides a controllable interface to edit these factors precisely.
method: Formulate relighting as a conditional image generation task and introduce attribute tokens that explicitly represent lighting factors (intensity, color, ambient illumination, diffuse level, 3D light positions).
Train a generator conditioned on these tokens using a large-scale synthetic dataset with ground-truth lighting annotations, augmented with a small real-image set for better realism/domain adaptation.
Allow continuous interpolation and independent manipulation of tokens at inference to produce precise, photorealistic relighting edits.
impact: Provides ML and vision practitioners a practical, interpretable mechanism for controllable relighting—useful for photo editing, AR/VR, data augmentation, and neural rendering workflows where precise lighting manipulation is required.
visual_elements: Before/after grid showing single-attribute edits (intensity, color, ambient, diffuse, light position) to demonstrate independent control

paper_title: TokenLight: Precise Lighting Control in Images using Attribute Tokens
paper_authors: Sumit Chaturvedi, Yannick Hold-Geoffroy, Mengwei Ren, Jingyuan Liu, He Zhang
